claims.claim_text: Ricursive Intelligence has released Ripple-65B Preview, an open-weight general-purpose variant of the proprietary model that powers its AI chip design platform.
claims.excerpt: Today, we release Ripple-65B Preview, a general-purpose variant of the proprietary model that powers our AI chip design platform.

claims.claim_text: Ricursive says the model was pretrained on 12 trillion tokens and supports up to 1M context length.
claims.excerpt: The model is pretrained on 12 trillion tokens with support for up to 1M context length.

claims.claim_text: Ricursive reports Ripple-65B Preview scored 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1, which it calls a U.S. open-weight state of the art, ahead of Reflection Beam 501B (80.1) and Meta Muse Spark Open 816B (76.4).
claims.excerpt: achieving U.S. open-weight state-of-the-art (80.52) on TerminalBench 2.1 and surpassing significantly larger US open-weight models such as Reflection Beam 501B (80.1), Meta Muse Spark Open 816B (76.4)

claims.claim_text: Ripple-65B Preview is available on Hugging Face, Together AI, GMI Cloud, OpenRouter, and Fireworks.
claims.excerpt: Ripple-65B Preview is available on Hugging Face, Together AI, GMI Cloud, OpenRouter, and Fireworks.

claims.claim_text: Ricursive says it developed and trained the model for $32M in full R&D cost, which it estimates is one-tenth the cost of the previous open-weight agentic coding leader.
claims.excerpt: we developed and trained Ripple-65B Preview for only $32M, which is one-tenth the cost of the previous open-weight SOTA on agentic coding, as estimated to the best of our knowledge.

claims.claim_text: Ricursive says it reached its TerminalBench 2.1 score with 1.4M RL rollouts, roughly 70x fewer than Reflection Beam.
claims.excerpt: We reached a TerminalBench 2.1 score of 80.5 with only 1.4M rollouts, roughly 70x fewer rollouts than Reflection Beam, the prior SOTA.

claims.claim_text: Ripple-65B Preview is a dense Transformer rather than a Mixture-of-Experts model, and Ricursive says it maintained 40% MFU through training.
claims.excerpt: we chose to train a modernized dense Transformer model rather than use Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) like other labs.

claims.claim_text: Ricursive says the model's small size lets it run efficiently on local devices such as NVIDIA DGX Spark.
claims.excerpt: The model’s small parameter envelope also enables it to run efficiently on local devices such as NVIDIA DGX Spark

claims.claim_text: Ricursive says its pretraining ladder changes improved code compute efficiency by up to 16x at 4B scale compared with the Olmo 3 ladder.
claims.excerpt: Together, the compounded changes improved compute efficiency on code as measured by dolma_stack CE by up to 16x at 4B model scale.

claims.claim_text: Ricursive says it bought no post-training data, building its own synthetic data pipelines instead.
claims.excerpt: We opted not to buy any posttraining data, instead devising our own synthetic data pipelines, quality filtering, and coverage metrics.
